nodes.summary: Even with duplicates, a cell never exceeds the rule enumeration length.
nodes.title: Computed CYK cell length bounded by the rule count

nodes.summary: A cell charges every rule, its test, and its possible output cons.
nodes.title: Cost bound for computing one CYK cell

nodes.summary: Exact cost of the empty-input production scan.
nodes.title: Exact cost of the CYK epsilon scan

nodes.summary: Output inspection is bounded; only binary productions scan splits.
nodes.title: Cost bound for the CYK production fit test

nodes.summary: All table cells, including invalid/default positions, have bounded membership-scan length. This invariant is proved from construction.
nodes.title: Every CYK table lookup is bounded by the rule count

nodes.summary: Exact charge for a full membership scan, including a failed scan.
nodes.title: Exact cost of a membership scan

nodes.summary: In the usual nonempty-input form, the bound is a constant times `n³`.
nodes.title: Indexed CYK costs a constant times $n^3$ on nonempty words

nodes.summary: Explicit cubic bound, for every word including the empty word. The coefficient depends only on the rule enumeration and equality costs; no semantic or assumed recurrence hypothesis occurs in this cost theorem.
nodes.title: Explicit cubic cost bound for indexed CYK

nodes.summary: The linear row-conversion charge uses the actual number of entries.
nodes.title: Length of a computed CYK row

nodes.summary: Row cost counts all starts, not only successful or distinct factors.
nodes.title: Cost bound for building one CYK row

nodes.summary: Each split pays for both indexed cell reads and both membership scans.
nodes.title: Cost bound for the CYK split scan

nodes.summary: Table cost includes allocation, every row conversion and every update. The memory-size hypothesis needed for split costs is discharged internally.
nodes.title: Cost bound for filling the indexed CYK table

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
